open: In the name of Allah. Assalamu alaikum, my dears. Come closer, tonight’s story is very beautiful.
s1a: Noah… Ilyas… do you remember? I promised you an important question. At the end of his life, the Prophet Yaqub called his sons and asked them: What will you worship after me?
s1b: And what did they say, Grandma?
s1c: That, I will tell you at the end of the story. Snuggle up nicely… Today I’ll tell you about the Prophet Yaqub, peace be upon him. He was the son of Ishaq and the grandson of Ibrahim.
s2a: Do you remember? The angels told Sara: after Ishaq comes Yaqub. And so it was. Ishaq was blessed with a son named Yaqub, and Allah made him a prophet too. Yaqub and his family lived in the desert.
s2b: And what did Yaqub teach his children?
s2c: The most important thing in the world! Allah says: “And Ibrahim instructed his sons to do the same, and so did Yaqub, saying: O my sons, indeed Allah has chosen for you this religion, so do not die except while you are Muslims.” That means: Ibrahim and Yaqub told their sons: stay with Allah, your whole life long.
s3a: Yaqub was a strong prophet. Allah says: “And remember Our servants, Ibrahim, Ishaq and Yaqub, those of strength and religious vision.” That means: they were strong in obeying Allah, and they saw the truth clearly. Yaqub prayed, did good, and guided people to Allah. Yaqub had many children, and one of them was named Yusuf.
s3b: One day, little Yusuf came to his father. Allah says: “When Yusuf said to his father: O my father, indeed I have seen eleven stars and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me!”
s3c: Eleven stars? What does that mean?
s3d: Yaqub was wise, and he understood that this vision was something great: “He said: O my son, do not relate your vision to your brothers or they will contrive against you a plan. Indeed Satan, to man, is a manifest enemy.” And he told him: your Lord will choose you, teach you the meaning of dreams, and complete His favor upon you and upon the family of Yaqub, as He completed it before upon your forefathers Ibrahim and Ishaq.
s4a: Then came a hard day. The brothers said to their father: Send Yusuf with us tomorrow! At first, Yaqub did not want to, then he let him go. In the evening, the brothers came back without Yusuf. They were crying and saying: A wolf ate him!
s4b: Oh Allah! And did Yaqub believe them?
s4c: No. Allah says: “And they brought his shirt with false blood upon it. Yaqub said: Rather, your souls have enticed you to something, so patience is most fitting. And Allah is the one sought for help against that which you describe.” That means: they brought Yusuf’s shirt with false blood on it. And Yaqub said: you made up this story; I will be beautifully patient, and Allah will help me.
s4d: Beautiful patience means: we are patient, and we don’t complain to people. And everything in our hearts, we tell to Allah.
s5a: Many years passed, and Yaqub never forgot Yusuf. He grieved for him so much that his eyes became white from grief. His sons said to him: You will keep remembering Yusuf until you become very ill, or die!
s5b: Allah says about Yaqub: “He said: I only complain of my suffering and my grief to Allah, and I know from Allah that which you do not know.” Then he said to them: “O my sons, go and find out about Yusuf and his brother and despair not of relief from Allah. Indeed, no one despairs of relief from Allah except the disbelieving people.” That means: look for Yusuf and his brother, and never lose hope in Allah’s mercy!
s5d: That, my dear, is a big story all of its own. I’ll tell it to you next time!
s6a: And now, the question I promised you. When Yaqub’s death drew near, he called his sons. Allah says: “Or were you witnesses when death approached Yaqub, when he said to his sons: What will you worship after me? They said: We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Ibrahim and Ismail and Ishaq, one God. And we are Muslims in submission to Him.”
s6b: Wait, Grandma… Ismail was Yaqub’s uncle, not his father!
s6c: Well done, my dear, you paid close attention! Arabs sometimes call an uncle “father”, because he is so close to the family. And look: Ibrahim, Ismail, Ishaq, Yaqub and his sons, all of them worshipped the One God, Allah.
s7a: Oh… they’ve fallen asleep. My dears… when you feel sad, remember Yaqub: be beautifully patient, and tell Allah everything that troubles you. Never despair of Allah’s mercy. And stay with Allah, your whole life long.
s7b: Next time, I’ll tell you about Yusuf… about a well, a prison and a king. And you, watching us right now: if you liked the story, ask your parents to subscribe to our channel, so you don’t miss the next story.
close: And you, dear fathers and mothers: subscribe to our channel, and share these stories with the people you love, so that together we pass on the beautiful message of Islam to our children.
final: Good night, my dears. I entrust you to Allah, with whom nothing entrusted is ever lost.
